what_its_for: Teduglutide is used to treat adults and children (1 year and older) with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS). Short Bowel Syndrome happens when part of your small intestine is missing or has been removed, making it hard for your body to absorb enough nutrients and fluids from food. This medicine helps your remaining intestine work better so your body can absorb more nutrients, and you may need less nutrition given through a vein (called parenteral nutrition or IV feeding).
how_to_take: Teduglutide comes as a powder in a vial that must be mixed with sterile water and given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection). Your healthcare team will teach you or your caregiver exactly how to mix and inject this medicine. Rotate your injection sites each day — you can use your stomach (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Do not inject into the same spot twice in a row. Always use a new needle for each injection. Inject once daily, at the same time each day.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 0.05 mg per kilogram of body weight injected once daily. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose based on your weight. For children, the dose is also based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not inject two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store the unmixed vials in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Do not freeze teduglutide. Keep it away from light. Once you mix the powder with sterile water, you must use it right away or within 3 hours if kept at room temperature. Throw away any unused mixed solution after 3 hours — do not save it for later. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid injecting into skin that is red, bruised, tender, hard, or scarred. Do not skip doses without talking to your doctor, as this can affect how well the medicine works. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medicines, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because teduglutide can change how your body absorbs other medications, which may mean your doses of other medicines need to be adjusted.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: sudden or severe stomach pain, bloating, or swelling; changes in your bowel movements (constipation or diarrhea getting much worse); rectal bleeding; a lump or pain near your rectum or anus; swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles (fluid buildup); shortness of breath or rapid weight gain; signs of a blocked bowel (no bowel movements, severe stomach cramping, vomiting); redness, pain, or swelling at your injection site that does not go away; or any new or unusual symptoms. Tell your doctor if you have a history of cancer, especially of the intestines or colon, before starting this medicine. Regular colonoscopies are required while on this medicine.
when_it_works: Teduglutide does not work overnight. Most people begin to see improvements in how much parenteral nutrition (IV feeding) they need after several weeks to months of treatment. Your doctor will regularly check your progress and may slowly reduce your IV nutrition as your intestine improves. It is important to keep taking the medicine every day as directed, even if you do not feel different right away.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if teduglutide is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Teduglutide is approved for children 1 year of age and older. Dosing is based on the child's weight. Kidney disease: If you have kidney problems, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose. Older adults: Older patients may need close monitoring, especially for fluid retention. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
